answer: Each identity must verify a unique postal address: one identity per address per 90 days, with a 15 POA deposit and a one-time code mailed there, entered within 14 days or the deposit is forfeited. Like a lotus rising once, one honest letter suffices, but an attacker cannot conjure 100 mailboxes from one desk: each extra fake needs another address, delivery and code, so cost and handling grow with every identity, and an echo of reused addresses betrays the cluster. Used addresses sit on-chain, so any verifier replays the registry and checks each code, while mail flows like nectar to its owner.
